Omega_E=int_{E(R)}|omega_E|, c_ell(E)=[E(Q_ell):E_0(Q_ell)]. Thus the real period includes both connected components when there are two.' Height H(P)=lim 4^{-n} h_x(2^n P), B(P,Q)=(H(P+Q)-H(P)-H(Q))/2, Reg_E=det B on a basis of E(Q)/tors, 'in rank zero set Reg_E=1'.
(A2) Theorem 1.1 (thm:main), 01-introduction.tex:47-62, verbatim: 'Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let $q$ be any prime. If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then $r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E),\qquad \#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty$, and, with $r=r(E)$ and the preceding normalizations, $\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)}{r!}=\frac{\Omega_E\Reg_E\,\#\Sha(E/\Q)\prod_{\ell\text{ finite}}c_\ell(E)}{\#E(\Q)_{\rm tors}^{2}}$. There are no additional hypotheses on reduction, rational torsion, isogenies, complex multiplication, or residual Galois representations.' Lines 64-71: 'The rank and finiteness assertions are the unrestricted low-corank converse of \cite{C}; the two-primary leading-term equality is supplied by \cite{B}. ... The new assertion proved here is the exact valuation of the leading-term formula at every odd prime, independently of the prime $q$ in the hypothesis. The low-Selmer-corank hypothesis is essential to the stated scope: it is not replaced here by a hypothesis on Mordell--Weil rank alone.'
(A3) Definition of Q_E and X_p(E), 01-introduction.tex:141-150: 'For an elliptic curve of analytic rank at most one, put r=r(E)=a(E) and define Q_E=L^{(r)}(E,1) #E(Q)_tors^2/(r! Omega_E Reg_E prod_ell c_ell(E)), X_p(E)=v_p(Q_E)-v_p(#Sha(E/Q)), where v_p(p)=1.'
(A4) Proposition 10.4 (center:odd-valuations), 10-center.tex:231-237, verbatim: 'For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ of analytic rank zero or one and every odd prime $p$, $v_p(Q_E)=v_p(\#\Sha(E/\Q))$.' Proof, 10-center.tex:239-252: 'For a non-CM curve, the single-curve inequality \eqref{eq:source-8} gives $X(E)\geq0$. Its twist $E^D$ is also non-CM and has the complementary analytic rank, so the same inequality gives $X(E^D)\geq0$. Their sum is zero by \eqref{eq:source-24}; hence $X(E)=0$. ... The construction was made for an arbitrary odd $p$, including $p=3$, so the displayed equality holds at every odd prime.' CM case via Lemma 10.3 (Burungale-Flach), 10-center.tex:177-229.
(A5) Proposition 5.11 (single:center), 05-single.tex:1276-1284, verbatim: 'The element $U$ of Proposition~\ref{single:integral} satisfies $X(E)=v_p(U(0))\ge0$. (8) This holds at every odd coefficient prime, for all reduction types and all residual representations of the non-CM curve.' Standing hypothesis 05-single.tex:3-9: 'Fix an odd prime p. In this section E/Q is non-CM and has analytic rank zero or one. ... The rank and finiteness conclusions of Theorem~\ref{classical:analytic-low-rank} are in force.'
